fullPassage: Douglass Houghton was a physician from Detroit who served as the state's first geologist. Lacking formal training in geology, he compensated with his tremendous energy, keen observation skills, and a deep passion for the natural world. He was also a talented speaker, winning audiences with his dynamic presentation style and charm. As a result of his geological surveys, the presence of copper deposits in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan became public knowledge. This led to a mining rush, often compared to the California gold rush. Despite the economic benefits of the mining boom, Houghton expressed genuine concern about the environmental and social consequences of uncontrolled mining. He advocated for careful and responsible resource management. Tragically, Houghton's life was cut short at the age of 36 when he drowned during a geological expedition on Lake Superior in 1845.
